name: Grammarly
summary: Grammarly provides AI-assisted writing and communication software for individuals and enterprises.
overview: Grammarly began as a writing assistant and has expanded into a broader productivity and AI communication platform. Its $13 billion 2021 equity valuation remains the latest disclosed priced valuation; a later $1 billion financing was non-dilutive and did not reset that mark.

facts.label: Equity financing
facts.note: 2021 round with Baillie Gifford and BlackRock participation.

facts.label: Later financing
facts.note: 2025 financing did not establish a new equity valuation.

bull_case: A trusted writing layer can become an embedded, cross-application AI productivity platform for consumers and enterprises.
bear_case: General-purpose AI assistants and office-suite incumbents may commoditize writing assistance and pressure retention or pricing.
directory_notes: Enterprise adoption and AI product differentiation.

intelligence.description: Grammarly provides AI-assisted writing and communication tools for consumers, teams, and enterprises.
company: Grammarly built a large installed base around writing suggestions and has broadened its product toward AI-assisted communication and productivity. Its distribution across browsers, desktops, and workplace software is a key strategic asset.

The company raised $200 million at a $13 billion valuation in November 2021. In 2025 it announced $1 billion of non-dilutive financing from General Catalyst; because that financing did not price equity, the profile retains the 2021 figure as the latest disclosed priced valuation.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Grammarly is a test of whether an established productivity application can preserve a trusted user relationship while generative AI shifts from a feature to the default interface for writing and knowledge work.

changed.text: Grammarly is founded as a writing-assistance company.
Secures $1B of non-dilutive financing to support expansion without establishing a new equity valuation.

takeaways: The $13B mark is a 2021 priced-equity valuation and should be read with that date in mind.
The 2025 $1B financing is non-dilutive, so it is not a new valuation event.
Distribution and user trust are important advantages in a crowded AI-writing market.
Competition from foundation-model providers and productivity suites is the central strategic risk.
